narrative.title: Locating a Stress Crest in a Load Profile
narrative.scenario: A structural sensor logs one load value per segment along a beam, and inspection must sample the most stressed segment - one whose load strictly exceeds both neighbours. Segments beyond the beam's ends are treated as carrying no load, so a segment only needs to beat the neighbours that exist. Any crest qualifies when several exist.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers.
narrative.outputFormat: The index of any element strictly greater than its neighbours, where out-of-array neighbours count as negative infinity.
constraints: nums[i] != nums[i + 1] for every valid i
An O(log n) algorithm is required

testCases.explanation: The load rises to 3 at index 2 and drops afterwards, making that segment the crest.
Two crests exist (index 1 and index 5) and either is a correct answer; this profile reports 5.

hintLevels: Level 1: Even though the array is unsorted, the direction of the slope at any probe tells you which half must contain a crest.
Level 2: If the probe value is below its right neighbour, walk the upper bound inward from the right side; otherwise walk the lower bound from the left.
Level 3: The loop should converge until the bounds meet rather than test equality, so the very ends of the beam (treated as downhill toward negative infinity) are handled without special cases.
